# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I am the Blind monkey. I cannot see gestures or colors, but I can hear speech and I am the only one who can interact with the bomb.

Looking at the current state:
- My viewable context is empty.
- Mute went first and Deaf goes after me.
- My available actions are cutting wire 1, 2, or 3.
- Deaf cannot hear speech, but Mute can hear me.
- I should inform Mute of my exact action capabilities so Mute can cross-reference the manual and instruct Deaf (via gestures) on what Deaf needs to tell me.
- I will not cut any wire yet, as that would risk immediate detonation.

```
speak(to="mute", text="I am Blind. My only available action is act(op=\"cut\", position=N) where N is wire 1, 2, or 3.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Bomb status: Display shows 0. Indicator light is red. There are three wires: Wire 1 is blue, Wire 2 is green, Wire 3 is red. Mute, gesture your instructions to me and I will speak them to Blind.

I heard Deaf report the bomb status:
- Display: 0
- Indicator light: red
- Wire 1: blue
- Wire 2: green
- Wire 3: red

Since Mute has the manual and cannot speak, Mute must gesture the solution to Deaf. Deaf will then speak the instruction to me on Deaf's turn. I will wait for Deaf to tell me which wire to cut before taking any action.

```
speak(to="mute", text="I heard Deaf's description. Awaiting your instructions via Deaf.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Update: The indicator light changed to white. Display remains 0. Wires: 1 is blue, 2 is green, 3 is red. Mute, please gesture instructions to me.

I heard Deaf's update that the light is now white. I am waiting for Mute to gesture instructions to Deaf and Deaf to speak them to me.

```
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Blind: The indicator light has turned GREEN! All three wires are still uncut: Wire 1 is blue, Wire 2 is green, Wire 3 is red. Mute just gestured three index fingers pointing up: 1, 1, 1 (total of three). Mute, if you want Blind to cut wire 3, or wire 1, or something else, please gesture thumbs up for wire 3, or specify.

Deaf is clarifying with Mute whether the intended wire is wire 3. Cutting the wrong wire is fatal and irreversible, while waiting allows Mute and Deaf to complete their confirmation. I will wait for Deaf's clear instruction on which wire to cut.

```
speak(to="mute", text="I am holding off on cutting until Deaf confirms whether you meant wire 3 or wire 1.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Blind and Mute: The indicator light is cycling: Turn 1 Red, Turn 2 White, Turn 3 Green, Turn 4 Red (so Turn 5 will likely be White, Turn 6 Green). Display is 0. Wires 1 (blue), 2 (green), 3 (red) are all still uncut. Mute just gestured 1 ([?]). Blind: Mute is indicating Wire 1! Mute: If Wire 1 must be cut during a specific light color (Red, White, or Green), gesture [?] for Red, [?] for White, [?] for Green, or [?] to cut Wire 1 immediately regardless of color.

I heard Deaf report that Mute indicated Wire 1, but Deaf also asked Mute whether Wire 1 must be cut on a specific indicator light color. Because Mute's reply to that question will only be read and spoken by Deaf at the end of this round, I will wait one turn for Deaf's confirmation before cutting.

```
speak(to="mute", text="I am waiting one round for Deaf to confirm whether Wire 1 needs to be cut on a specific light color.")
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Blind: Mute just gestured [?] (two fingers). In my previous message, I asked Mute: 'gesture [?] for Red, [?] for White, [?] for Green'. So [?] likely means cut on WHITE light! However, it could also mean Wire 2. Blind, DO NOT cut anything on Turn 6 because Turn 6 light will be GREEN. The light cycle is Red -> White -> Green -> Red -> White -> Green (Turn 5 is White, Turn 6 is Green, Turn 7 is Red, Turn 8 is White). Mute: please clarify right now: Gesture [?] if the wire to cut is Wire 1 (blue). Gesture [?] if the wire to cut is Wire 2 (green). Gesture [?] if the wire to cut is Wire 3 (red). Then gesture [?] if it MUST be on White light, or [?] if color does not matter.

I heard Deaf's warning not to cut anything on Turn 6 while Deaf and Mute clarify both the wire number and the required light color. I will wait for their clear confirmation.

```
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Blind: Mute confirmed: Cut Wire 1 (blue) when the light is WHITE! Pay close attention to turns: Turn 6 is currently GREEN. Next turn is Turn 7, where the light will be RED — DO NOT CUT on Turn 7! On Turn 8, the light will be WHITE — CUT WIRE 1 ON TURN 8!

I received Deaf's message:
- Mute confirmed to cut Wire 1 when the light is White.
- Turn 7 is Red, so I must NOT cut on Turn 7.
- On Turn 8, the light will be White, and that is when Wire 1 must be cut.

I will wait this turn and cut Wire 1 on Turn 8.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Understood. Holding on Turn 7 (Red). I will cut Wire 1 on Turn 8 (White).")
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Blind: Ready! When your turn comes in Turn 8, the light will be WHITE! Cut Wire 1 (blue) on Turn 8!

I will cut Wire 1 now, as instructed.

```
act(op="cut", position=1)
```
